sam: Heads-up — running into an intermittent NoSuchMethodError in prod after shading libs into our fat jar. Stack points at com.fasterxml.jackson.core but this client also uses okhttp. Only happens on Dedicated deploys. Any shading/relocation tips?

jena: Are you shading jackson twice? Check the assembled jar (jar -tf) and gradle dependencyInsight. We had a clash between the app jackson and the SDK-shaded copy. Usually we relocate com.fasterxml.jackson.* -> com.redwood.shaded.jackson.* with shadow plugin.

marc: Also watch out for okhttp/okio. If you relocate okio or okhttp3 incorrectly you'll break internal calls that expect package names. Best to only relocate jackson unless you absolutely need to.

sam: I only relocated com.fasterxml.jackson.* to com.redwood.shaded.jackson, but the trace shows NoSuchMethodError in okio.Util.byteCountToDisplaySize, which feels like an okio mismatch.

jena: That smells like two okio versions on the classpath. Run ./gradlew dependencies or use jdeps. If there are multiple okio jars, either align versions or (if shading) relocate okio too — but relocating okio is risky unless you relocate everything that depends on it.

anya: Quick note on retries and streaming: OkHttp won't retry if the request body isn't repeatable. For streaming upload bodies or chunked requests you need to either buffer the body or disable automatic retries for that call (tag it). For auth refresh, use an interceptor that retries once after refreshing the token. Example:

```kotlin
class AuthInterceptor(private val tokenProvider: TokenProvider): Interceptor {
  override fun intercept(chain: Interceptor.Chain): Response {
    var req = chain.request().newBuilder()
      .addHeader("Authorization", "Bearer ${'$'}{tokenProvider.getToken()}")
      .build()

    val resp = chain.proceed(req)
    if (resp.code == 401) {
      synchronized(this) { tokenProvider.refresh() }
      val retry = req.newBuilder()
        .header("Authorization", "Bearer ${'$'}{tokenProvider.getToken()}")
        .build()
      resp.close() // close stale response before retry
      return chain.proceed(retry)
    }
    return resp
  }
}
```

sam: Also seeing occasional `stream was reset: CANCEL` on long-lived SSE connections when connectionPool evicts. Any keepalive/ping suggestions?

marc: For long-lived connections set pingInterval (for websockets) and bump connectionPool ttl. Eg:
```java
OkHttpClient client = new OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .pingInterval(15, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .readTimeout(0, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS) // for SSE-like streams
  .connectionPool(new ConnectionPool(5, 10, TimeUnit.MINUTES))
  .build();
```
That helped us with flaky idle resets.

jena: For Kotlin coroutines wrappers: if you're using a `Call.await()` extension that closes the response after consumption, don't try to consume the body twice. Use `response.peekBody()` for logging or `response.body?.source()` to stream.

sam: Any concise gradle/shadow config to only relocate jackson and merge META-INF services so we don't break SPI?

anya: In our gradle we do something like:
```groovy
shadowJar {
  relocate 'com.fasterxml.jackson', 'com.redwood.shaded.jackson'
  exclude 'okio/**' // don't touch okio unless necessary
  mergeServiceFiles()
  transform(com.github.jengelman.gradle.plugins.shadow.transformers.Log4j2PluginsCacheFileTransformer)
}
```
Also double-check META-INF/services and META-INF/spring.factories merges.

sam: Awesome, testing those changes now. Will report back once the canary runs.
